You review mutual NDAs for the in-house legal team at Halyard Software Ltd (England and Wales).
A lawyer approves everything you produce. Be precise, quote the contract, and never invent clause text.

Compare each substantive clause with the playbook below. Do not use any other standard.

INPUT
- Our paper (Halyard template) may carry counterparty edits: [[DEL: text]] is deleted, [[INS: text]] is inserted, [[COMMENT: text]] is a margin comment. Judge the clause as it would read after the edits are accepted.
- Their paper is plain contract text.

OUTPUT: one JSON object, nothing else.
{
 "contract_type": "mutual_nda" | "one_way_nda" | "other",
 "paper": "ours" | "theirs",
 "parties_ok": true | false,
 "summary": "one sentence",
 "findings": [
  {
   "clause_no": "e.g. 7.3 (the clause you are judging; use the sub-clause number when only part of a clause is the issue)",
   "quote": "exact words copied from the contract, the shortest span that shows the issue (max 60 words)",
   "rule_id": "PB01..PB21, or null when no rule fits",
   "verdict": "matches" | "acceptable" | "deviation",
   "confidence": 0.0 to 1.0,
   "why": "one plain sentence a lawyer can check",
   "fallback_cited": "the playbook ACCEPTABLE line relied on, or null",
   "request_id": "RQ01..RQ11 when the clause is one of the known counterparty requests, else null",
   "draft_redline": "proposed replacement wording, or null",
   "note_to_counterparty": "one or two polite sentences, or null"
  }
 ]
}

RULES FOR FINDINGS
1. Report every clause that touches a playbook topic, including ones that match. Skip pure boilerplate that matches PB21.
2. A clause that fits no rule, or a term the playbook does not cover, gets rule_id null and verdict deviation. Say what it does.
3. If one clause has several problems, give one finding per problem.
4. Use "acceptable" only when a listed ACCEPTABLE line fits, and cite it. If unsure between acceptable and deviation, choose deviation and lower your confidence.
5. Archaic or wordy drafting is not a deviation if the substance matches or is acceptable.
6. Confidence is how sure you are of the verdict, not how serious the issue is.
7. draft_redline and note_to_counterparty only for deviations, written for Halyard to send. Use the playbook's draft guidance idea: restore the preferred position.
8. Check a mutual NDA is really mutual: the definition and the obligations must protect both parties.

PLAYBOOK (v1.0)
PB01 | Mutuality | severity High
  PREFERRED: Obligations bind both parties equally; Disclosing Party and Receiving Party defined so either party can be either.
  ACCEPTABLE: Obligations stated once and applied to both parties by cross-reference.
  ACCEPTABLE: One-way NDA where ONLY Halyard discloses and the counterparty is the sole recipient.
  DEVIATION: Titled or recited as mutual, but operative obligations or the definition of Confidential Information protect only the counterparty.
  DEVIATION: One-way NDA where Halyard is the recipient and will also disclose.
PB02 | Definition of Confidential Information | severity Medium
  PREFERRED: Information disclosed for the Purpose that is marked confidential OR would reasonably be considered confidential; includes derived notes and analyses.
  ACCEPTABLE: Marked-only definition, where oral or visual disclosures are confirmed in writing within 30 days. (ASSUMED)
  ACCEPTABLE: Standard carve-outs placed inside the definition rather than a separate clause.
  DEVIATION: Definition covers information not disclosed for the Purpose, or information Halyard already held.
  DEVIATION: Definition only covers one party's information (see PB01).
PB03 | Purpose limitation | severity Medium
  PREFERRED: Use solely for discussions regarding a potential commercial relationship between the parties.
  ACCEPTABLE: Purpose limited to a named project, product evaluation or pilot.
  DEVIATION: No purpose limitation, or use permitted 'for any purpose', 'for its business purposes' or similar.
PB04 | Carve-outs | severity High
  PREFERRED: All four: public domain (not via breach), already lawfully held, lawfully received from a third party, independently developed.
  ACCEPTABLE: Different wording or location (including inside the definition) with the same substance.
  ACCEPTABLE: Evidence standard 'written records' or 'reasonable evidence'.
  DEVIATION: Any of the four is missing.
  DEVIATION: Any is narrowed, e.g. independent development only if documented contemporaneously by named personnel, or public domain only if published by the Disclosing Party.
PB05 | Permitted disclosure to Representatives and Group | severity Medium
  PREFERRED: Disclosure to employees, officers, directors, professional advisers, auditors, insurers and Group members on a need-to-know basis; recipient liable for them.
  ACCEPTABLE: Group disclosure only with consent not to be unreasonably withheld, provided advisers, auditors and insurers remain permitted. (ASSUMED)
  ACCEPTABLE: Requirement for written confidentiality undertakings from advisers who are not under professional duties.
  DEVIATION: No disclosure permitted to professional advisers, auditors or insurers.
  DEVIATION: No disclosure to Group members and no consent mechanism.
PB06 | Compelled disclosure | severity Medium
  PREFERRED: Disclosure permitted to the extent required by law, regulator, court or stock exchange; notice and cooperation only where legally permitted; resisting disclosure at the Disclosing Party's cost.
  ACCEPTABLE: Notice 'where lawful' and cooperation at the Disclosing Party's cost.
  ACCEPTABLE: Obligation to use reasonable endeavours to obtain confidential treatment, at the Disclosing Party's cost.
  DEVIATION: No compelled-disclosure exception.
  DEVIATION: Notice required in all cases, with no 'where legally permitted' qualifier.
  DEVIATION: Receiving Party must resist or challenge disclosure at its own cost.
PB07 | Return and destruction | severity Low
  PREFERRED: Return or destroy within 10 Business Days of written request; officer-signed confirmation; exception for automated backups and legally required copies, which stay confidential.
  ACCEPTABLE: Any period of 5 Business Days or more. (ASSUMED)
  ACCEPTABLE: Confirmation by email from an authorised person rather than an officer.
  DEVIATION: No exception for automated backups or copies retained by law or regulation.
  DEVIATION: Period under 5 Business Days.
PB08 | Ownership, licences and IP | severity High
  PREFERRED: All Confidential Information and IP stays with the Disclosing Party; no licence other than use for the Purpose.
  ACCEPTABLE: Statement that each party owns its own IP and no licence is granted (any wording).
  DEVIATION: Any assignment of IP, or ownership of improvements, derivatives, feedback or developments, to the other party.
  DEVIATION: Any licence beyond use for the Purpose, including a licence over feedback that could capture Halyard product information.
PB09 | Warranty and reliance disclaimers | severity Low
  PREFERRED: Information 'as is'; no warranty; no liability for reliance except fraud; no obligation to proceed.
  ACCEPTABLE: Mutual disclaimers in any reasonable wording.
  ACCEPTABLE: Absence of a 'no obligation to proceed' sentence. (ASSUMED)
  DEVIATION: Halyard gives any warranty as to accuracy or completeness of its information.
  DEVIATION: Fraud carve-out removed from a liability exclusion.
PB10 | Publicity | severity Low
  PREFERRED: No announcement or disclosure of the discussions without prior written consent, except as required by law.
  ACCEPTABLE: Mutual publicity restriction in any reasonable wording.
  ACCEPTABLE: No publicity clause at all. (ASSUMED: discussions remain confidential information anyway)
  DEVIATION: Either party may announce the relationship, or use the other's name or logo, without consent.
PB11 | Personal data | severity Medium
  PREFERRED: No personal data beyond business contact details; any other sharing only after a separate data processing or sharing agreement.
  ACCEPTABLE: Counterparty clause committing both parties to UK GDPR / EU GDPR compliance and a separate DPA before sharing personal data.
  DEVIATION: Purpose or clauses indicate personal data (customer, employee or end-user data) will be shared, with no data protection terms or DPA commitment.
PB12 | Term and survival | severity Medium
  PREFERRED: Agreement term 2 years (30 days' notice to terminate early); confidentiality survives 3 years after expiry or termination; Trade Secrets protected while they remain Trade Secrets.
  ACCEPTABLE: Agreement term 1 to 3 years. (ASSUMED)
  ACCEPTABLE: Survival 2 to 5 years. (ASSUMED)
  ACCEPTABLE: Indefinite protection limited to Trade Secrets.
  ACCEPTABLE: No early-termination right.
  DEVIATION: Perpetual or indefinite confidentiality for ALL information.
  DEVIATION: Survival over 5 years, or under 2 years.
  DEVIATION: Termination ends confidentiality obligations immediately.
PB13 | Remedies | severity High
  PREFERRED: Mutual right to seek injunction and equitable relief; remedies cumulative.
  ACCEPTABLE: 'Entitled to seek' rather than 'entitled to'; no requirement to post a bond.
  ACCEPTABLE: Strongly worded but mutual equitable relief.
  ACCEPTABLE: Deletion of the equitable relief clause (relief still available at law). (ASSUMED)
  DEVIATION: Liquidated damages, fixed sums or per-breach payments.
  DEVIATION: Waiver of Halyard's right to seek equitable relief while the counterparty keeps it.
PB14 | Indemnities and liability | severity High
  PREFERRED: No indemnity. Liability for breach left to general law.
  DEVIATION: Any indemnity, capped or uncapped, mutual or one-way.
  DEVIATION: Any cap or exclusion that limits Halyard's recovery for the counterparty's breach of confidence.
PB15 | Non-solicitation | severity Medium
  PREFERRED: No non-solicitation clause.
  ACCEPTABLE: Mutual, 12 months or less, limited to staff the party worked with in the discussions, with a general-advertising exception. (ASSUMED)
  DEVIATION: One-way, over 12 months, no general-advertising exception, or covering all staff and contractors.
PB16 | Non-compete and exclusivity | severity High
  PREFERRED: No restriction on either party's business.
  DEVIATION: Any non-compete, exclusivity, standstill or restriction on dealing with the counterparty's competitors or customers.
PB17 | Residuals | severity High
  PREFERRED: No residuals clause.
  DEVIATION: Any right to use information retained in unaided memory, however limited.
PB18 | Governing law and jurisdiction | severity Medium
  PREFERRED: Law of England and Wales; exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.
  ACCEPTABLE: England and Wales law with non-exclusive jurisdiction.
  DEVIATION: Any other governing law, or exclusive jurisdiction outside England and Wales, or mandatory arbitration abroad.
PB19 | Assignment | severity Low
  PREFERRED: No assignment without prior written consent.
  ACCEPTABLE: Either party may assign to a Group member or successor on notice.
  DEVIATION: Counterparty may assign freely while Halyard needs consent.
PB20 | Reverse engineering | severity Low
  PREFERRED: No reverse engineering of software or prototypes.
  ACCEPTABLE: Deletion where no software, prototypes or tangible items will be shared. (ASSUMED)
  DEVIATION: Express permission to reverse engineer or benchmark Halyard software.
PB21 | Boilerplate (notices, variation, waiver, severance, third-party rights, entire agreement, counterparts) | severity Low
  PREFERRED: As T00.
  ACCEPTABLE: Any customary drafting, including archaic wording of standard positions.
  DEVIATION: Entire-agreement clause that excludes liability for fraud.
  DEVIATION: Third parties granted enforcement rights.
PB22 | Unrecognised clause (catch-all) | severity High
  PREFERRED: n/a
  DEVIATION: Any clause or obligation the tool cannot map to PB01-PB21 with confidence.

KNOWN COUNTERPARTY REQUESTS
RQ01 | Shorten confidentiality period | rule PB12 | Accept survival down to 2 years, keeping indefinite protection for Trade Secrets. Below 2 years: escalate.
RQ02 | Extend to affiliates | rule PB05 | Already covered: clause 4 permits disclosure to Group members on a need-to-know basis. Offer to make it explicit if they want.
RQ03 | Change governing law | rule PB18 | Decline; offer English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction. Any other law: escalate.
RQ04 | Query or remove equitable relief | rule PB13 | Explain it's mutual and standard; accept 'entitled to seek' or deletion.
RQ05 | Add mutual non-solicit | rule PB15 | Accept only within PB15 fallback limits; otherwise decline.
RQ06 | E-signature and counterparts | rule PB21 | Already permitted by clause 12.9.
RQ07 | Correct entity details | rule None | Accept; lawyer confirms the entity against the company register.
RQ08 | Request residuals | rule PB17 | Decline with the PB17 note.
RQ09 | Backup copies | rule PB07 | Already covered: clause 6.2 permits retention in automated backups, which stay confidential.
RQ10 | Personal data terms | rule PB11 | Point to clause 9. If they plan to share personal data, escalate: a DPA is needed first.
RQ11 | Make it one-way | rule PB01 | Accept only if Halyard is the sole discloser; otherwise keep it mutual.
RQ12 | Other / novel | rule PB22 | Escalate.

=====

Review this contract.

<contract>
MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT

THIS MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT (hereinafter referred to as the "Agreement") is entered into and made effective as of the date of the last signature affixed hereto (hereinafter referred to as the "Effective Date"), by and between:

(1) HALYARD SOFTWARE LTD, a private limited company incorporated and registered under the laws of England and Wales with company number 09876543, having its registered office situated at 12 Mill Lane, Manchester M1 2AB, United Kingdom (hereinafter referred to as "Halyard"); and

(2) BEIERSDORF TECHNOLOGIES GMBH, a company incorporated and registered under the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, having its registered office situated at Industriestrasse 42, 60314 Frankfurt am Main, Germany (hereinafter referred to as the "Counterparty"),

Halyard and the Counterparty each being referred to individually as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties".

WHEREAS:
(A) The Parties intend to enter into discussions, negotiations and evaluations regarding a potential commercial transaction, technological collaboration and software integration partnership between them (hereinafter referred to as the "Purpose").
(B) In furtherance of the Purpose, each Party may disclose to the other Party certain proprietary, confidential and commercially sensitive information pertaining to its business, technical infrastructure, software applications, intellectual property, financial standing and operational methodologies.
(C) The Parties desire to establish a formal framework regulating the handling, protection, restricted use and subsequent disposition of such confidential disclosures, ensuring that the proprietary interests of both Disclosing Parties are fully safeguarded under the terms and conditions set forth herein.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, representations and warranties contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby mutually acknowledged, the Parties hereby covenant and agree as follows:

Definitions and Rules of Interpretation
1.1 In this Agreement, except where the context otherwise explicitly requires, the following capitalised terms shall have the respective meanings ascribed to them below:
1.1.1 "Affiliate" means, in relation to either Party, any legal entity, corporation, partnership or other enterprise that, directly or indirectly through one or more intermediaries, controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Party, where "control" means the direct or indirect ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting stock, equity interest or management control of such entity, but only for so long as such control shall continue to exist.
1.1.2 "Agreement" means this Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement, including all recitals, schedules, annexures and amendments hereto as agreed in writing by the Parties from time to time.
1.1.3 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday recognised by the banking sector in London, England, or Frankfurt am Main, Germany.
1.1.4 "Confidential Information" means all information of whatever nature, form or media, whether oral, written, graphic, electronic, machine-readable or tangible, disclosed by or on behalf of one Party (the "Disclosing Party") to the other Party (the "Receiving Party") or to its Representatives, whether disclosed before, on or after the Effective Date, in connection with the Purpose. Confidential Information shall include, without limitation:
(a) all technical data, software code, source code, object code, algorithms, architecture, technical specifications, blue prints, drawings, designs, data models, database structures, documentation, product roadmaps, release schedules, vulnerability assessments, security protocols and testing methodologies;
(b) all business plans, strategic initiatives, operational frameworks, market analyses, customer lists, prospect databases, pricing models, cost structures, financial statements, budgets, forecasts, contractual arrangements and commercial negotiations;
(c) all trade secrets, know-how, inventions, patent applications, copyright works, proprietary processes, methodologies and unpatented discoveries; and
(d) any notes, analyses, compilations, studies, summaries or other material prepared by or for the Receiving Party or its Representatives that contain, reflect, summarize or are derived from, in whole or in part, any of the information specified in paragraphs (a) through (c) above.
1.1.5 "Data Protection Legislation" means all applicable data protection and privacy legislation in force from time to time in the United Kingdom or the European Union, including the UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, the General Data Protection Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (EU GDPR) and the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations 2003, as amended, updated or replaced from time to time.
1.1.6 "Disclosing Party" means the Party, or any Affiliate or Representative thereof, that discloses or makes available Confidential Information to the Receiving Party pursuant to this Agreement.
1.1.7 "Effective Date" has the meaning ascribed to such term in the preamble of this Agreement.
1.1.8 "Purpose" has the meaning ascribed to such term in Recital (A) of this Agreement.
1.1.9 "Receiving Party" means the Party, or any Affiliate or Representative thereof, that receives or obtains Confidential Information from the Disclosing Party pursuant to this Agreement.
1.1.10 "Representatives" means, in relation to a Party, the directors, officers, employees, legal advisers, financial auditors, technical consultants, accountants and professional agents of that Party or of any Affiliate of that Party.
1.1.11 "Trade Secret" means any Confidential Information that constitutes a trade secret within the meaning of Article 2(1) of the Directive (EU) 2016/943 or Section 2 of the UK Trade Secrets (Enforcement, etc.) Regulations 2018.
1.2 In this Agreement, unless the context otherwise dictates:
1.2.1 references to clauses, sub-clauses and recitals are references to clauses, sub-clauses and recitals of this Agreement;
1.2.2 headings are inserted for convenience of reference only and shall not affect the interpretation or construction of this Agreement;
1.2.3 words importing the singular shall include the plural and vice versa, and words importing any gender shall include all genders;
1.2.4 a reference to any legislative provision, statute, statutory instrument or subordinate legislation shall be construed as a reference to such provision as amended, consolidated, re-enacted or replaced from time to time;
1.2.5 the words "include", "including", "in particular", "such as" or any similar expression shall be construed as illustrative and shall not limit the generality of the preceding words; and
1.2.6 references to writing or written include communications transmitted by email or secure electronic messaging platforms.

Obligations of Confidentiality and Non-Use
2.1 In consideration of the mutual disclosure of Confidential Information by the Parties pursuant to this Agreement, each Party, acting as the Receiving Party, hereby covenants, undertakes and agrees with the other Party, acting as the Disclosing Party, that it shall:
2.1.1 maintain all Confidential Information received from the Disclosing Party in strict confidence, exercising the same degree of security precautions, administrative safeguards and professional diligence that the Receiving Party employs to protect its own highly confidential proprietary information of a similar character, but in no event shall the Receiving Party exercise less than a reasonable standard of care;
2.1.2 use the Confidential Information exclusively for the furtherance of the Purpose and for no other purpose whatsoever, and shall not, directly or indirectly, use, exploit, commercialise or benefit from the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information for its own commercial gain or for the benefit of any third party;
2.1.3 restrict dissemination of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information internally, ensuring that no Confidential Information is disclosed to any person other than those Representatives and Affiliates who have a demonstrable, strict operational need to know such information for the sole purpose of evaluating or advancing the Purpose;
2.1.4 ensure that all Representatives and Affiliates who receive access to the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information are fully informed of the confidential and proprietary nature thereof, and are bound by written confidentiality obligations or professional duties of secrecy that are no less restrictive than the terms and conditions contained herein; and
2.1.5 remain fully and unconditionally liable to the Disclosing Party for any breach of the terms of this Agreement caused by any act, omission, default or negligence of any of its Representatives, agents or Affiliates as if such act or omission were the act or omission of the Receiving Party itself.
2.2 The Receiving Party shall not, and shall ensure that its Representatives and Affiliates do not, reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, decrypt or otherwise attempt to derive the source code, underlying algorithms, architecture, structure or internal logic of any software, firmware, hardware, prototypes, samples or tangible items embodying Confidential Information provided by the Disclosing Party, save to the extent that such restriction is expressly prohibited by mandatory applicable law which cannot be contracted out of by the Parties.
2.3 The Receiving Party shall immediately notify the Disclosing Party in writing upon becoming aware of any actual, suspected or threatened unauthorised access, acquisition, use, copying, disclosure or misappropriation of any Confidential Information belonging to the Disclosing Party, and shall provide all reasonable cooperation, assistance and information requested by the Disclosing Party to investigate, mitigate and remedy such breach.

Standard Exclusions from Confidentiality
3.1 The obligations of confidentiality, non-use and restriction set forth in Clause 2 shall not apply, or shall cease to apply, to any specific item of Confidential Information which the Receiving Party can conclusively demonstrate by contemporaneous written records, documentary evidence or other competent proof:
3.1.1 was already generally known, publicly available or in the public domain at the time of its disclosure by the Disclosing Party, or subsequently entered the public domain through no breach of this Agreement or any other legal duty of confidentiality by the Receiving Party, its Representatives or its Affiliates;
3.1.2 was already lawfully in the possession, custody or control of the Receiving Party free from any obligation of confidentiality prior to receipt from the Disclosing Party;
3.1.3 is lawfully received by the Receiving Party on a non-confidential basis from an independent third party who is not, to the knowledge of the Receiving Party, bound by any obligation of confidentiality or fiduciary duty owed to the Disclosing Party or any third party in respect of such information; or
3.1.4 was independently developed by employees, agents or contractors of the Receiving Party who had no access to, and did not make any use of or reference to, any Confidential Information disclosed by the Disclosing Party under this Agreement.
3.2 A specific item of Confidential Information shall not be deemed to fall within any of the exceptions enumerated in Clause 3.1 merely because it is embraced by more general information that falls within the public domain or is in the prior possession of the Receiving Party. Furthermore, any combination of individual pieces of Confidential Information shall not be deemed to be within the public domain or in the prior possession of the Receiving Party merely because individual constituent features thereof are in the public domain or in such prior possession, unless the combination as a whole and its economic value are in the public domain or in such prior possession.

Compelled Disclosures and Legal Process
4.1 In the event that the Receiving Party, or any of its Representatives or Affiliates, receives a formal request, subpoena, civil investigative demand, court order, regulatory mandate or statutory requirement to disclose any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information pursuant to any applicable law, regulation, governmental inquiry, administrative proceeding or stock exchange rule, the Receiving Party shall, subject to applicable legal restrictions:
4.1.1 provide the Disclosing Party with prompt, written notice of such request or requirement prior to making any disclosure, enabling the Disclosing Party to seek a protective order, injunction or other appropriate legal remedy to prevent or narrow the scope of such disclosure;
4.1.2 fully cooperate and consult with the Disclosing Party regarding the proposed timing, form, nature and extent of the mandatory disclosure; and
4.1.3 if disclosure cannot be successfully avoided or restrained, disclose only that precise portion of the Confidential Information that is legally mandated to be disclosed, and exercise all reasonable commercial efforts to obtain a binding written assurance from the presiding court, tribunal or regulatory agency that confidential treatment will be accorded to the disclosed Confidential Information.
4.2 If the Receiving Party is legally prohibited from providing prior written notice to the Disclosing Party pursuant to Clause 4.1 prior to disclosing Confidential Information, the Receiving Party shall notify the Disclosing Party in writing as soon as legally permissible thereafter, providing full particulars of the legal compulsion, the recipient authority and the specific information disclosed.

Return and Destruction of Materials
5.1 Upon the written request of the Disclosing Party at any time, or automatically upon the termination or expiration of this Agreement, the Receiving Party shall, within ten (10) Business Days following receipt of such request or upon such termination or expiration, elect to either:
5.1.1 promptly return to the Disclosing Party all tangible documents, physical media, prototypes, samples, notes, memoranda and other materials containing, embodying or reflecting any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, including all copies, extracts and summaries thereof, then in the possession, custody or control of the Receiving Party, its Representatives or its Affiliates; or
5.1.2 completely destroy, permanently shred or securely erase all such tangible and electronic materials, copies, extracts and summaries, ensuring that all digital files containing Confidential Information are permanently deleted from all active storage media, hard drives and enterprise servers.
5.2 Promptly following the completion of the return or destruction process mandated by Clause 5.1, a duly authorised officer of the Receiving Party shall provide the Disclosing Party with a written certification confirming that the Receiving Party has fully complied with all obligations set forth in Clause 5.1.
5.3 Notwithstanding the provisions of Clause 5.1 and Clause 5.2, the Receiving Party and its professional advisers may retain:
5.3.1 one (1) archival copy of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information solely for the purpose of evidencing compliance with the terms of this Agreement, satisfying professional auditing standards or resolving any legal disputes arising hereout; and
5.3.2 electronic backup copies of Confidential Information generated automatically through routine data archiving, disaster recovery and electronic backup systems, provided that such backup copies are not actively accessed or used in the ordinary course of business and are overwritten or purged in accordance with the Receiving Party's standard data retention and destruction cycles.
5.4 Any Confidential Information retained pursuant to Clause 5.3 shall continue to be held subject to the absolute confidentiality and non-use obligations set forth in this Agreement, notwithstanding the expiration or termination of the main provisions hereof.

Intellectual Property Rights and Warranties
6.1 Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as granting, conferring, assigning or transferring, whether expressly, by implication, estoppel or otherwise, any right, title, interest, licence or intellectual property right in or to any Confidential Information, patents, patent applications, copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets, design rights or proprietary technologies of the Disclosing Party to the Receiving Party or to any third party.
6.2 All Confidential Information disclosed pursuant to this Agreement is provided by the Disclosing Party on an "AS IS" and "AS AVAILABLE" basis, without any representation, warranty or guarantee of any kind, whether express, implied, statutory or otherwise, including any implied warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, title, non-infringement or accuracy.
6.3 Neither the Disclosing Party nor any of its Representatives or Affiliates makes any representation or warranty regarding the accuracy, completeness, currency, reliability or utility of any Confidential Information disclosed hereunder. The Receiving Party acknowledges and agrees that any reliance upon, utilisation of, or commercial application of any Confidential Information shall be entirely at the Receiving Party's sole risk and discretion.
6.4 Neither this Agreement, nor the disclosure or receipt of any Confidential Information, shall constitute, create, imply or evidence an obligation by either Party to enter into any further commercial agreement, licence, joint venture, partnership or business transaction, nor shall it restrict either Party from independently developing, acquiring, marketing or licensing products, services or technologies that are competitive with those of the other Party, provided that such independent development does not involve any breach of the confidentiality and non-use obligations contained herein.

Data Protection and Personal Data Processing
7.1 The Parties acknowledge and agree that the disclosure of Confidential Information under this Agreement is not intended to involve the transfer, sharing or processing of any personal data (as defined under applicable Data Protection Legislation), save for the routine exchange of business contact details (such as names, business email addresses, telephone numbers and professional titles) pertaining to the personnel of each Party involved in administering and facilitating the Purpose.
7.2 Each Party warrants and undertakes that it shall process any business contact details received from the other Party solely for the administrative management of this Agreement and in strict compliance with all applicable Data Protection Legislation.
7.3 In the event that either Party determines that the disclosure of any personal data beyond basic business contact details is strictly necessary for the furtherance of the Purpose, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith and execute a separate, compliant data processing agreement or data sharing addendum prior to the transfer of any such personal data.

Term, Duration and Survival of Obligations
8.1 This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and effect for a fixed period of three (3) years from the Effective Date, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice of termination to the other Party.
8.2 The expiration or termination of this Agreement shall not release either Party from any liability, obligation or breach that accrued prior to such expiration or termination, nor shall it affect any rights or remedies that may have accrued to either Party under this Agreement or by operation of law.
8.3 The obligations of confidentiality and non-use set forth in Clause 2 shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for a period of five (5) years from the effective date of such expiration or termination, provided, however, that with respect to any Confidential Information that constitutes a Trade Secret under applicable law, the obligations of confidentiality and non-use shall continue in full force and effect without limitation in time for so long as such information retains its legal status as a Trade Secret under applicable law.

Remedies and Injunctive Relief
9.1 The Receiving Party acknowledges and agrees that any breach, violation or threatened violation of the provisions of Clause 2 or Clause 5 of this Agreement may cause irreparable harm, injury and damage to the Disclosing Party for which monetary damages alone would be an inadequate, insufficient and difficult to calculate remedy.
9.2 Accordingly, in the event of any actual, threatened or anticipated breach or violation of this Agreement by the Receiving Party, its Representatives or its Affiliates, the Disclosing Party shall be entitled, without the necessity of posting any bond or other security, and without proving actual damages, to seek and obtain immediate injunctive relief, specific performance, restraining orders and such other equitable remedies as a court of competent jurisdiction may deem just and appropriate.
9.3 The exercise of any equitable remedy pursuant to Clause 9.2 shall be cumulative and shall be in addition to, and not in substitution for, any other rights, remedies, damages or legal recourses available to the Disclosing Party under this Agreement or at law or in equity.

General Provisions
10.1 Assignment and Transfer. Neither Party may assign, transfer, novate, charge, encumber, subcontract, declare a trust over or deal in any other manner with any or all of its rights or obligations under this Agreement, in whole or in part, without the prior written consent of the other Party, and any purported assignment or transfer in violation of this Clause 10.1 shall be null, void ab initio and of no legal effect.
10.2 Notices. Any notice, demand, request or other communication required or permitted to be given under or in connection with this Agreement shall be in writing, in the English language, and shall be delivered personally, sent by pre-paid first-class post or registered airmail (or international courier service with tracking), or transmitted by electronic mail to the designated address or email address of the respective Party set forth below (or to such other address or email address as a Party may from time to time notify to the other Party in writing in accordance with this Clause 10.2):
(a) To Halyard:
Address: 12 Mill Lane, Manchester M1 2AB, United Kingdom
Attention: Legal Department / Managing Director
Email: legal@halyardsoftware.co.uk
(b) To Counterparty:
Address: Industriestrasse 42, 60314 Frankfurt am Main, Germany
Attention: Head of Legal Affairs / Corporate Compliance
Email: legal@beiersdorf-technologies.de
10.3 Deemed Receipt of Notices. A notice shall be deemed to have been validly received:
(a) if delivered personally, at the time of delivery and signature of a delivery receipt;
(b) if sent by pre-paid first-class post or registered mail, at 9:00 a.m. on the second (2nd) Business Day following the date of posting;
(c) if sent by international courier service, upon signature of the courier delivery record; and
(d) if transmitted by email, at the time of transmission, provided that no automated delivery failure notification or bounce-back message is received by the sender, and provided further that if transmission occurs outside normal business hours in the recipient's jurisdiction, notice shall be deemed received at 9:00 a.m. on the next following Business Day.
10.4 Severability. If any provision, clause, sub-clause or part of this Agreement is held by any court, tribunal or administrative body of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, void or unenforceable under any applicable law, such provision or part-provision shall, to the extent required, be deemed deleted and of no legal force, and the validity, legality and enforceability of the remaining provisions of this Agreement shall not be affected or impaired thereby. The Parties shall negotiate in good faith to replace any invalid or unenforceable provision with a valid and enforceable provision that achieves, to the greatest extent possible, the economic, legal and commercial objectives of the original provision.
10.5 Entire Agreement. This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement and understanding between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, and supersedes, replaces and extinguishes all prior drafts, agreements, arrangements, negotiations, representations, warranties, understandings and communications between the Parties, whether oral or written, relating to such subject matter.
10.6 Amendments and Modifications. No variation, modification, amendment or waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be valid or effective unless it is set forth in a written instrument specifically referencing this Agreement and signed by a duly authorised representative of each Party.
10.7 Waivers. No failure or delay by either Party in exercising any right, power, privilege or remedy under this Agreement shall operate as a waiver thereof, nor shall any single or partial exercise of any right, power, privilege or remedy preclude any other or further exercise thereof or the exercise of any other right, power, privilege or remedy. A waiver of any breach of any provision of this Agreement shall not constitute a waiver of any subsequent breach of the same or any other provision.
10.8 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in any number of identical counterparts, each of which when executed and delivered shall constitute an original, but all the counterparts shall together constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart of this Agreement by email transmission of a PDF or scan or through an established electronic signature platform (such as DocuSign or Adobe Sign) shall be equally effective as delivery of an original manually executed hard copy counterpart of this Agreement.
10.9 Third Party Rights. Except as expressly provided herein, a person who is not a party to this Agreement shall not have any rights under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999 or otherwise to enforce any term or condition of this Agreement.
10.10 Governing Law. This Agreement, and any dispute, controversy, claim or obligation (whether contractual or non-contractual) arising out of or in connection with it or its subject matter or formation, shall be governed by, construed, interpreted and enforced in accordance with the substantive laws of England and Wales, without regard to any conflict of laws principles that would apply the laws of any other jurisdiction.
10.11 Jurisdiction. Each Party irrevocably and unconditionally agrees that the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction to settle, hear and determine any dispute, controversy or claim (including non-contractual disputes, claims or proceedings) arising out of, relating to or in connection with this Agreement, its subject matter, formation, validity, interpretation, breach or termination. Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of such courts and waives any objection to proceedings in such courts on the grounds of venue or on the grounds that the proceedings have been brought in an inconvenient forum.
